questions.q: A wire of length $L$~is hanging from a fixed support. The length changes to ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ when masses $1$ kg and $2$ kg are suspended respectively from its free end. Then the value of $L$ is equal to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Hooke's law,& $∆ L = \dfrac{FL}{AY} ⇒ ∆ L ∝ F$. Therefore,

$\dfrac{{L}_{2} - L}{{L}_{1} - L} = \dfrac{{m}_{2}g}{{m}_{1}g} = \dfrac{2}{1}⇒ L = 2{L}_{1} - {L}_{2}$

questions.q: Two wires A and B are made of same material having ratio of lengths $\frac{L_A}{L_B}=\frac{1}{3}$ and their diameters ratio $\frac{d_A}{d_B}=2$. If both the wires are stretched using same force, what would be the ratio of their respective elongations?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{B}}}=2$
$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{A}}}$ and $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{B}}}$
Given, $F_A=F_B$ and $Y_A=Y_B$
$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{A}}}}{\frac{\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{B}}}}= \left(\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)$\$left(\frac{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{A}}}\right)
\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)\left(\frac{\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{~d}_{\mathrm{B}}^2}{\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{~d}_{\mathrm{A}}^2}\right)=\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{A}}}\right)^2$
\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\r$right)^2=\frac{1}{12}$

questions.q: The Young's modulus of a steel wire of length $6m$~and cross-sectional area $3{mm}^{2}$, is $2 \times {11}^{11}N / m^{2}$ . The wire is suspended from its support on a given planet. A block of mass $4$ kg is attached to the free end of the wire. The acceleration due to gravity on the planet is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of its value on the earth. The elongation of wire is (Take $g$ on the earth $= 10m / s^{2}$ ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The external force or tension& \left(F\right)$~acting on the wire is its own weight. It is given by

~$\begin{cases}F & = & mg \\ = & 4kg \times \dfrac{10}{4}ms^{- 2} \\ = & 10N\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the Young's modulus of the material of the wire is given by

$\begin{cases}Y & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ L}{L}} \\ = & \dfrac{FL}{∆ LA} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )\end{cases}$

where,~$A$~is the cross-sectional area,~$L$~is the original length and~$∆ L$~is the elongation of the wire.

Substitute the given values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required elongation of the wire.

$\begin{cases}2 \times {10}^{11}N / m^{2} & = & \dfrac{10N \times 6m}{∆ L \times 3{mm}^{2} \times \dfrac{1m^{2}}{{10}^{6}{mm}^{2}}} \\ ∆ L & = & \dfrac{10N \times 6m}{2 \times {10}^{11}N / m^{2} \times 3{mm}^{2} \times \dfrac{1m^{2}}{{10}^{6}{mm}^{2}}} \\ = & 0 . 0001m \times \dfrac{{10}^{3}mm}{1m} \\ = & 0 . 1mm\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Speed of a transverse wave on a straight wire (mass $6.0g,$ length $60$ cm and area of cross-section $1.0mm^{2}$~ is $90\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. If the Young's modulus of wire is $16 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$, the extension of wire over its natural length is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}$
$⇒ T = \muv^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{\muv^{2}}{A} = Y\dfrac{∆ l}{l}$
$⇒ ∆ l = \dfrac{\muv^{2}l}{AY}$
After substituting value of $\mu, v, l, A$ and $Y$ we get
$∆ l = 0 . 3mm$

questions.q: An aluminium rod with Young’s modulus $Y = 7 . 0 \times {10}^{10}Nm^{- 2}$ undergoes elastic strain of $0 . 04 %$. The energy per unit volume stored in the rod in $SI$ unit
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The data given is&

$Y = 7 \times {10}^{10}Nm^{- 2}\text{and}\dfrac{∆ l}{l} = \dfrac{0 . 04}{100}$

Young's modulus is given by the ratio of stress and strain,

$Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}} = \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l}$

The energy stored is given as~

$E = \left(\dfrac{YA}{2l}\right) ∆ l^{2} ⇒ E = \left(\dfrac{YA}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{∆ l}{l}\right)2 \times l . . . ( i )$

The energy per unit volume can be written from equation (i)

$\dfrac{E}{V} = \dfrac{Y}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{∆ l}{l}\right)2 . . . ( ii )$

Substituting the values in equation (ii)

$\dfrac{E}{V} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 7 \times {10}^{10} \times \dfrac{0 . 04 \times 0 . 04}{104} = 56 \times {10}^{2}$

questions.q:
The area of cross section of the rope used to lift a load by a crane is $2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}$. The maximum lifting capacity of the crane is $10$ metric tons. To increase the lifting capacity of the crane to 25 metric tons, the required area of cross section of the rope should be
(take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since breaking stress (Maximum lifting capacity) is the property of material, so it will remain same.

Now, breaking stress$= \dfrac{Maximumliftingcapacity}{Areaofcrosssectionofrope}$

$⇒ \dfrac{10}{2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} = \dfrac{25}{A}$

$A = 625 \times {10}^{- 6}$

$= 6 . 25 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}$

questions.q: Young's moduli of two wires $A$ and $B$ are in the ratio $7: 4$ . Wire $A$ is $2m$ long and has radius $R .$ Wire $B$ is $1.5m$ long and has radius $2mm .$ If the two wires stretch by the same length for a given load, the value of $R$ is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Strain $= ∆ l / l$
Stress $= F / A$
Young’s modulus $= \dfrac{Stress}{Strain} = \dfrac{F / A}{ \left(∆ l / l\right)} = \dfrac{F}{A}\left(\dfrac{l}{∆ l}\right)
\dfrac{{Y}_{A}}{{Y}_{B}} = \left(\dfrac{{l}_{A}}{{A}_{A}}\right)\left(\dfrac{{A}_{B}}{{l}_{B}}\right) = \dfrac{7}{4}
\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi{r}_A^{2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{\pi{r}_B^{2}}{1.5}\right) = \dfrac{7}{4}
${r}_A^{2} = $\dfrac{2}{1.5 \times 7} \times {\left(2mm\right)}^{2}
${r}_{A} = 1.7mm

questions.q: A 3 m long wire of radius 3 mm shows an extension of 0.1 mm when loaded vertically by a mass of 50 kg in an experiment to determine Young's modulus. The value of Young's modulus of the wire as per this experiment is $\mathrm{P} \times 10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$, where the value of P is: (Take  \left.\mathrm{g}=3 \pi \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{50 \mathrm{~g}}{\pi \mathrm{r}^2}=\mathrm{y} \cdot \frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell} \\ & \frac{50 \times 3 \pi}{\pi \times\left(3 \times 10^{-3}\right)^2}=\mathrm{P} \times 10^{11} \times \frac{0.1 \times 10^{-3}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}=\frac{50 \times 3 \times 3}{3^2 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{11} \times 0.1 \times 10^{-3}} \\ & \mathrm{P}=5\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Four identical hollow cylindrical columns of mild steel support a big structure of mass $50 \times {10}^{3}kg .$~The inner and outer radii of each column are $50$ cm and $100$ cm respectively. Assuming uniform local distribution, calculate the compression strain of each column.
[use $Y = 2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}Pa, g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} = \dfrac{mg}{4AY}$
$= \dfrac{50 \times {10}^{3} \times 9 . 8}{4\pi\left({100}^{2} - {50}^{2}\right) \times {10}^{- 4} \times 2 \times {10}^{11}} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{5}}{4 \times \pi \times 150 \times 50 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 2 \times {10}^{11}}$
$\dfrac{ΔL}{L} = \dfrac{1}{12\pi} \times {10}^{- 5} = 2 . 60 \times {10}^{- 7}$

questions.q: A wire of length $L$~and radius $r$~is clamped rigidly at one end. When the other end of the wire is pulled by a force$f$, its length increases by $l$. Another wire of same material of length $2L$~and radius $2r$~is pulled by a force $2f$. Then the increase in its length will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Young's modulus is same for both the wires since the material is same.

For the first wire,

$Y = \dfrac{fL}{\pir^{2}l} . . . ( i )$

For the second wire,

$Y = \dfrac{2f ( 2L )}{4\pir^{2}l '} . . . ( ii )$

Dividing (i) by (ii)

$\dfrac{fL}{\pir^{2}l} \times \dfrac{4\pir^{2}l '}{4fL} = 1 ⇒ l ' = l$

questions.q: Young's modules of material of a wire of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is $Y .$ If the length of the wire is doubled and cross-sectional area is halved then Young's modules will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Young’s modulus depends on the material not length and cross-sectional area. So Young’s modulus will remain same irrespective of the dimension of the wire.

questions.q:
The force required to stretch a wire of cross-section $1{cm}^{2}$ to double its length will be :

(Given Yong's modulus of the wire $= 2 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The wire is stretched to& double its length. Therefore, if the length of the wore was& $l$, change in the length~$∆ l = l$.

Applying Hooke's law,

$Y = \dfrac{stress}{strain} = \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l} ⇒ F = \dfrac{YA ∆ l}{l} = YA ⇒ F = 2 \times {10}^{11} \times 1 \times {10}^{- 4} = 2 \times {10}^{7}N$

$= 2 \times {10}^{11} \times {10}^{- 4} \left(\dfrac{2l - l}{l}\right)

$= 2 $\times {10}^{7}$N$

$

questions.q: Under the same load, wire A having length $5 . 0m$~and cross section $2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}m^{2}$ stretches uniformly by the same amount as another wire $B$ of length $6 . 0m$ and a cross section of $3 . 0 \times {10}^{- 5}m^{2}$ stretches. The ratio of the Young's modulus of wire $A$ to that of wire $B$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Elongation in uniform wire under load is given by,& $\Deltal = \dfrac{Fl}{SY},$~where $S$~is area of cross-section.

As~$F$ is same for both wire and $\Deltal$ is also same, we can write

$\dfrac{\Deltal}{F} = \dfrac{l}{SY} ⇒ \dfrac{lA}{{S}_{A}{Y}_{A}} = \dfrac{lB}{{S}_{B}{Y}_{B}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5}{\left(2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}\right) \times {Y}_{A}} = \dfrac{6}{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 5}\right) \times {Y}_{B}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{YA}{YB} = 1$

questions.q: A wire of length $L$ and radius $r$ is clamped at one end. If its other end is pulled by a force $F$, its length increases by $l$. If the radius of the wire and the applied force both are reduced to half of their original values keeping original length constant, the increase in length will become:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the Young's modulus of the material of the wire, in the first case, can be written as

$Y = \dfrac{F\pir^{2}}{lL} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$F = Y\pir^{2} \times $\dfrac{l}{L} . . . \left(2\right)$

For the second case, the Young's modulus is given by

$Y = $\dfrac{F / 2\pir^{2} / 4}{l 'L} . . . \left(3\right)$

From equation (3), it follows that

$F = Y\dfrac{l '}{L} \times2 \times \dfrac{\pir^{2}}{4} . . . \left(4\right)$

From equations (2) and (4), it implies that

$Y\pir^{2} \times \dfrac{l}{L} = Y\dfrac{l '}{L} \times 2 \times \dfrac{\pir^{2}}{4} ⇒ l ' = 2l$

questions.q:
One end of a metal wire is fixed to a ceiling and a load of $2$ kg hangs from the other end. A similar wire is attached to the bottom of the load and another load of $1$ kg hangs from this lower wire. Then the ratio of longitudinal strain of upper wire to that of the lower wire will be

[Area of cross section of wire $= 0 . 005{cm}^{2}, Y = 2 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$ and $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, change in length is given by $\Delta L = \dfrac{FL}{AY}$

Therefore, strain required $\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} = \dfrac{F}{AY}$

Now the ratio will be, $\dfrac{\Delta{L}_{1}{L}_{1}}{\Delta{L}_{2}{L}_{2}} = \dfrac{F1}{{F}_{2}} = \dfrac{T1}{{T}_{2}} = \dfrac{30}{10} = 3$

questions.q:
The volume contraction of a solid copper cube of edge length 10 cm , when subjected to a hydraulic pressure of $7 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~Pa}$, would be ____ $\mathrm{mm}^3$.
(Given bulk modulus of copper $=1.4 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}}{\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{V}=\frac{7 \times 10^6}{1.4 \times 10^{11}} \times\left(10 \times 10^{-2}\right)^3 \\ & \Delta \mathrm{~V}=50 \mathrm{~mm}^3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two slabs with square cross section of different materials $(1,2)$ with equal sides $(l)$ and thickness $\mathrm{d}_1$ and $\mathrm{d}_2$ such that $\mathrm{d}_2=2 \mathrm{~d}_1$ and $l \gt \mathrm{d}_2$. Considering lower edges of these slabs are fixed to the floor, we apply equal shearing force on the narrow faces. The angle of deformation is $\theta_2=2 \theta_1$. If the shear moduli of material 1 is $4 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$, then shear moduli of material 2 is $\mathrm{x} \times 10^9 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$, where value of $x$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Deformation angle
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \theta_1=\theta_2 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \frac{\sigma_1}{\eta_1}=\frac{\sigma_2}{\eta_2}
\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2\left(\frac{\mathrm{~F}}{\ell \mathrm{~d}_1 \eta_1}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\ell \mathrm{d}_2 \eta_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \eta_2=\frac{\eta_1}{4}=1 \times 10^9 \Rightarrow x=1\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
In an experiment to determine the Young's modulus, steel wires of five different lengths ($1, 2, 3, 4$~and $5$) but of same cross-section \left(2{mm}^{2}\right)$ were taken and curves between extension and load were obtained. The slope (extension/load) of the curves were plotted with the wire length and the following graph is obtained. If the Young's modulus of given steel wires is $x \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$, then the value of $x$ is _____ .

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that, Young's modulus is& $Y = \dfrac{FL}{A ∆ L}$, where,~$F$~is force or load acting on wire,~$A$~is~cross-section area,~$L$~is length and~$∆ L$~is extension in length.

Now, from given graph, the slope of the line is $= \dfrac{\dfrac{\Delta L}{W}}{L} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}}{W} = \dfrac{1}{YA}$

$⇒ Y = \dfrac{1}{\left(slope\right)A}$

Thus, Young's modulus of the steel wires is $Y = \dfrac{1}{2 \times {10}^{- 6}\left(0 . 25 \times {10}^{- 5}\right)}$

$⇒ Y = 2 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$.

Therefore,~$x = 2$.
